items.title: Section: Five Destinies, Four Postures, Twelve Trades, Eight Transformations — And the Four Formless Aggregates Fully Explained at Last

items.zh: 謂異熟生，五趣別故，五種差別。若威儀路，威儀別故，四種差別。若工巧處，十二事差別故，即十二種差別。異生、聲聞、獨覺、菩薩、如來差別故，為嬉戲、為利他、身語變化差別故，當知變化八種差別。由此差別即攝餘事，故不別說。又異熟生，一向無記；二，三可得；一，有二種。若依伎樂，以染污心發起威儀，是染污性；若依寂靜，即是善性。若依染著發起工巧，是染污性；若善加行所起工巧，即是善性。為引導他，或為利益諸有情故，而起變化，當知是善，此無染污。
items.en: Karma-ripened aggregates are distinguished into five, according to the five destinies. Ordinary posture is distinguished into four, according to the postures. Livelihood-craft is distinguished into twelve, according to its activities. Distinguished by ordinary being, hearer-disciple, solitary realiser, bodhisattva, and buddha, by amusement or benefit for others, and by bodily or verbal transformation, one should know transformation is distinguished into eight. Furthermore, karma-ripened aggregates are invariably neutral; two — posture and craft — admit all three moral qualities; transformation is of two kinds. If posture arises through music and dance with a defiled mind, it is defiled; if through stillness, it is wholesome. If craft arises through attachment, it is defiled; if through wholesome effort, it is wholesome. Transformation displayed to guide or benefit beings is wholesome, and never defiled.

items.title: Section: A New Beginning — How the Five Aggregates Relate to the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 復次，如是五蘊幾諦所攝？又此諸諦幾蘊所攝？當知三諦、五蘊更互相攝。滅諦、諸蘊互不相攝。由滅諦性是彼寂靜所顯故。
items.en: Furthermore, how many of the truths subsume these five aggregates? And how many of the aggregates do these truths in turn subsume? One should know that three truths and the five aggregates mutually subsume one another. The truth of cessation and the aggregates do not mutually subsume one another, since cessation's own nature is precisely their quiescence made manifest.

items.title: Section: Sixteen Aspects of the Four Truths — Four Inverted Views, and Four Cravings That Generate Them

items.zh: 問：如聲聞地已說於四諦中有十六行觀，何故於苦諦為四行觀？答：為欲對治四顛倒故。謂初一行對治初一顛倒，次一行對治次二顛倒，後二行對治後一顛倒。問：何故於集諦為四行觀？答：由有四種愛故。此四種愛，當知由常、樂、淨、我愛差別故，建立差別；初愛為緣，建立後有愛；第二、第三愛為緣，建立喜貪俱行愛及彼彼希樂愛；最後愛為緣，建立獨愛，當知此愛隨逐自體。
items.en:
Question: as already explained in the Stage of the Hearer's Vehicle, why does the truth of suffering have four aspects of contemplation? Answer: to counter four inverted views. The first aspect counters the first inversion; the second counters the next two; the last two counter the final inversion.
Question: why does the truth of origin have four aspects? Answer: because of four kinds of craving, established through craving for permanence, pleasure, purity, and self respectively. The first craving establishes craving for future existence; the second and third establish both a craving that clings to a pleasant object already had, and one that reaches for a pleasant object not yet had; the last establishes craving itself, the one called simply craving, following one's own individual being.

items.title: Section: Four Cravings Named in Full — Self-Love, the Wish for More Life, and Longing for What Is Not Yet Had

items.zh: 又愛云何？謂於自體親昵藏護。後有愛云何？謂求當來自體差別。喜貪俱行愛云何？謂於現前、或於已得可愛色聲香味觸法起貪著愛。彼彼希望愛云何？謂於所餘可愛色等起希求愛。
items.en: What is craving itself? Intimate attachment and protectiveness towards one's own being. What is craving for future existence? Seeking a distinct embodiment yet to come. What is craving that clings with relish? Attachment arising towards a pleasing object already obtained or currently present. What is craving that reaches with longing? Attachment arising towards a pleasing object not yet obtained.

items.title: Section: Cessation's Four Faces and the Path's Four Faces — Each Precisely Undoing a Craving

items.zh: 問：何故於滅諦為四行觀？答：由四種愛滅所顯故。問：何故於道諦為四行觀？答：由能證彼四愛滅故。
items.en: Question: why does the truth of cessation have four aspects? Answer: they are revealed through the ending of the four cravings. Question: why does the truth of the path have four aspects? Answer: because the path is what actually brings about the ending of those four cravings.

items.title: Section: "Nothing to Be Found" — Searching for a Self and Discovering Only Seven Recurring Phenomena

items.zh: 復次，如聲聞地已說壞等十種行相，此中，無所得云何？謂唯有根、唯有境界，唯有彼所生受、唯有彼所生心、唯有計我我想、唯有計我我見、唯有我我言說戲論，除此七外，餘實我相了不可得。
items.en: Furthermore, as already explained in the Stage of the Hearer's Vehicle, there are ten aspects such as decay... within these, what is nothing-to-be-found? There is only the faculty, only its object, only the feeling it generates, only the mind it generates, only the notion of self and what is mine, only the view of self and what is mine, and only the verbal proliferation built from self and what is mine — apart from these seven, no further, genuinely real self-characteristic can ever be found.

items.title: Section: No Self-Mastery, and Why an Arhat Feels No Grief When Everything Falls Apart

items.zh: 不自在云何？謂眾緣生、無常、苦相所攝諸行，離我相故。問：此十行相，由何行相攝壞苦耶？答：由結行相及變壞增上所起憂惱，當知是壞苦性，非唯變壞。已離憂者，雖復遇彼不為害故。問：何等行相攝苦苦耶？答：由不可愛行相。問：何等行相攝行苦耶？答：由不安隱行相。
items.en: What is lack of self-mastery? The conditioned, impermanent, unsatisfactory phenomena that constitute the aggregates, being free of any self-characteristic. Answer: it is the grief and distress arising through the aspect of bondage and the dominant force of decay, not decay alone, that constitutes the suffering of decay. One who has already left grief behind is unharmed even when encountering it. Question: what aspect subsumes the suffering of pain? Answer: unloveliness. Question: what aspect subsumes the suffering of formations? Answer: insecurity.

items.zh: 復次，如經言：生苦乃至略攝五取蘊苦。

items.title: Section: Eight Familiar Sufferings Sorted Into Three — And Why Even the Form Realm's Bliss Still Counts as Suffering

items.zh: 如是諸苦相，幾苦苦攝？謂初五。幾壞苦攝？謂中二。幾行苦攝？謂後一。復次，初七，苦苦攝；彼所對治淨妙煩惱，壞苦攝；最後一，行苦攝。
items.en: How many of these eight sufferings belong to the suffering of pain? The first five. How many to the suffering of decay? The middle two. How many to the suffering of formations? The last one. Furthermore, in another reading, the first seven belong to the suffering of pain; the afflictions concerning the pure and excellent states that oppose them belong to the suffering of decay; the last belongs to the suffering of formations.

items.zh: 由世尊言：入變壞心。又作是言：由蓋纏故，領彼所生心諸憂苦。故知煩惱壞苦故苦道理成就。復次，

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Suffering From Scripture, and Why the Four Cravings Resist Being Neatly Filed Away

items.zh: 如經言：有四種苦。一者、生苦，二、緣內苦，三、緣外苦，四、麁重苦。問：此中何行攝何苦？何苦攝何行？答：初行、初苦，展轉相攝；次有三行，與第二苦展轉相攝；次有三行，與第三苦展轉相攝；最後一行，與最後苦展轉相攝。前所說愛自性差別建立集諦四種行相，當知為生今果差別四種苦故。
items.en: As scripture says, there are four kinds of suffering: birth-suffering, suffering conditioned internally, suffering conditioned externally, and the suffering of underlying heaviness. Question: which aspect corresponds to which suffering? Answer: the first corresponds to the first; the next three correspond to the second; the next three correspond to the third; and the last corresponds to the last. The four cravings already described as establishing the origin truth's four aspects should be understood as generating the present result's four distinct sufferings.

blocks.text: A new topic: how the five aggregates relate to the four noble truths, and the sixteen aspects under which the truths are contemplated.
Ripening is always neutral; transformation is good if done for others' benefit, neutral if for amusement.
Suffering, origin, and path and the five aggregates include one another; cessation does not, being revealed by their stilling. Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and origin are the contaminated aggregates.
Impermanence counters taking things as permanent; suffering counters taking them as pleasant and pure; emptiness and non-self counter taking them as self.

Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to permanence, wishing to exist forever, one seeks a life to come; the other two cravings arise towards experienced objects. Love of one's own particular body is "self-craving".
The four aspects of cessation are revealed by the ending of four cravings; the path realises that ending. Master Cháng Bǎi: one need not pair them mechanically.
"Apart from these seven, no real self-characteristic can be found": faculty, object, feeling, mind, and the rest.
It is the distress arising through affliction together with decay, not decay alone. Master Cháng Bǎi: some, with wisdom, see things decay without distress.

The first five belong to the suffering of pain, the middle two to change, the last to conditioning. Master Cháng Bǎi: taking conditioned things as pure and craving them, the mind changes for the worse; that is the suffering of change. (Untranslated, 0605a23: the Blessed One spoke of "entering a changed mind", and of distress born of the hindrances; so the suffering of change is established through affliction.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: one should not read the categories mechanically and force every item into a box.
"Decay alone is not the suffering of change; it is decay plus affliction." The arhat sees things end and is not distressed.

quiz.q: Which moral qualities do ripening, posture and craft, and transformation admit?
options: ripening is always neutral; posture and craft admit all three; transformation two, good for others' benefit and neutral for amusement
ripening admits all three; posture and craft are always neutral; transformation too admits all three, for it can harm, and so can be defiled
all four are always neutral, with no good or evil
all four admit all three
quiz.why: The treatise says ripening is invariably neutral, two admit all three qualities, and one is of two kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: transformation is good if for others' benefit, and neutral if for amusement; and the same posture differs as defiled or pure according to intention. The English "it is unwholesome" for 染汙性 is narrower, since 染汙 includes the obscured-neutral.

quiz.q: How do the five aggregates and the four truths subsume each other?
options: all four truths and the aggregates mutually subsume, cessation also falling under formations
three truths and the aggregates mutually subsume; cessation does not, being revealed by their quiescence
only suffering subsumes with the aggregates, not origin or the path
the truths and aggregates do not subsume each other at all
quiz.why: The treatise says three truths and the five aggregates mutually subsume one another, while cessation does not, being revealed by their quiescence. Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and origin belong to the contaminated aggregates, and the path to the uncontaminated; cessation is the quiescence of the aggregates, and so is not one of them.

quiz.q: How do the four aspects of suffering counter the four inverted views?
options: the first two counter the first inversion; the third the next two; the last the final inversion
the first counters the first inversion; the second the next two; the last two the final inversion
each aspect counters one inversion, one by one, four to four, with no combining
all four together counter one inversion, the others left to origin
quiz.why: The treatise says the first aspect counters the first inversion, the next counters the following two, and the last two the final inversion. So impermanence counters taking as permanent, suffering counters taking as pleasant and pure, and, as Master Cháng Bǎi says, emptiness and selflessness counter taking the aggregates as self.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain craving with relish, craving with longing, and craving for future existence?
options: future craving is for what is present; relish for the next life; longing for the past, all three being self-craving, not object-craving
all three are only towards the future
all three are wholesome aspiration
future craving seeks another life from clinging to permanence; relish is for what is present or had; longing for what is not yet had; the last two are object-craving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the clinging to permanence, wishing to exist forever, one seeks a life to come; the two others arise from notions of pleasure and purity towards experienced objects, and are object-craving. The treatise says relish is for what is present or obtained, and longing for the rest, which is why 餘 means what has not been obtained.

quiz.q: 獨愛 is "solitary craving," and the next section has "craving itself." How does the lecture explain it?
options: it is defiled longing for one's own life-form, love of one's own inner body, self-craving; "solitary" does not convey this
獨愛 is the love of pratyekabuddhas, found only in them, so "solitary" exactly conveys it as the treatise means
獨愛 is the loneliness of being alone
獨愛 is loving one person exclusively
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: defiled longing for one's own life-form, love of one's particular inner body, is called 獨愛; intimate protection of one's own life-form is self-craving, also called self-love. So 獨 means individual and inner. "Solitary craving" does not show this, and the different rendering "craving itself" in §47 hides that they are one craving.

quiz.q: Why do cessation and the path each have four aspects? Must the four cravings match them one by one?
options: they are revealed by, and realise, the ending of four cravings; the Sub-commentary's pairing need not be followed, since any contemplation on the path cuts them
the match must be one by one, the treatise expressly tying each aspect to each craving, or practice would lose its order
they arise from the four inversions, unrelated to craving
they are the four mindfulnesses, unrelated to cessation
quiz.why: The treatise gives only one sentence: the four aspects are revealed through the ending of four cravings, and the path realises that ending. Master Cháng Bǎi: the pairing in the Sub-commentary need not be followed; contemplating any phenomena on the path cuts the four cravings. The English overview presents a one-to-one matching as the treatise's, which comes from another sūtra.

quiz.q: What are the seven in "nothing to be found"?
options: form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness, space, and nirvāṇa, apart from which no self exists, these seven including everything
the seven limbs of awakening
faculty, object, resulting feeling, resulting mind, notion of self, view of self, and verbal proliferation of self
the seven kinds of pride
quiz.why: The treatise says that apart from these seven, no real self-characteristic can be found. Master Cháng Bǎi: faculty and object belong to form, resulting feeling to feeling, resulting mind to consciousness, the notion of self to perception, and the view of self to formations; 我我 means self and what belongs to self, which the English rightly brings out.

quiz.q: Is the suffering of decay merely change? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: not change alone; one with wisdom of impermanence who feels no affliction at change has no suffering of decay
yes: wherever things change there is suffering of decay, with or without affliction, arhats too having it
it belongs only to form, unrelated to mind
it is simply ageing and death
quiz.why: The treatise says it is the distress arising through affliction together with decay that is the suffering of decay, not decay alone. Master Cháng Bǎi: not only the decay of phenomena is called this; some have wisdom of impermanence and feel no affliction at decay, and for them there is no such suffering. The question of who has left grief is variously answered in the lecture, so it is not asked here.

quiz.q: How are the eight sufferings sorted into the three?
options: the first two under pain; the middle five under decay, birth through death all being change; the last under formations
the first five under suffering of pain; the middle two under decay; the last under formations
the first under formations; the other seven under pain
all eight under suffering of pain
quiz.why: The treatise says the first five belong to the suffering of pain, the middle two to decay, and the last to formations. Master Cháng Bǎi: for the unliberated, when lovely things decay, part, or a pursuit fails, distress arises, which is the suffering of decay; and the five clinging aggregates, flowing on towards death from birth, are never secure.

quiz.q: The English has "the pure, excellent state that opposes them, when clung to." Where is the subject misplaced?
options: the Chinese says the noble path falls under decay, since even it decays, so "state" should be "noble path"
the Chinese says 淨妙煩惱: the craving born of a notion of purity; the English turns the affliction into a pure opposing state
the Chinese says nirvāṇa, which the English omits
nothing is misplaced: affliction itself is pure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when beings take a notion of purity towards conditioned things and give rise to craving, the mind at that moment changes for the worse, and this is the suffering of decay. So what belongs to decay is the affliction. The English adds "when clung to" and makes a "pure, excellent state" the subject, moving the fault from the affliction to what it clings to.

quiz.q: The close of §52 in English has "not as mapped one to one." Is this the treatise? What is its source?
options: yes: the treatise has this sentence and goes on to explain why, so the English faithfully keeps it, needing no note
no: it comes from the Sub-commentary's 非定別配 and the Commentary; the English writes the gloss into the treatise
no: it comes from the Treatise on Consciousness-Only
no: it comes from the translator's life of Xuánzàng
quiz.why: The Chinese ends with "for the sake of generating the present result's four kinds of suffering." The qualification comes from the Sub-commentary's 非定別配. Master Cháng Bǎi: one should not read the words mechanically and force the four cravings onto the four aspects and four sufferings. The point is sound, but it belongs in a note, not in the translated text.
